verdict.rationale: Ubuntu's own docs say you can 'replace your current operating system' and that it is 'easy to install in place of Windows'. The documentation set covers creating a bootable USB, installing Ubuntu Desktop, and handling Windows-specific blockers (BitLocker, Intel RST/AHCI) during installation. A community user also reports doing a clean 18.04 install. Missing for 10: detailed first-party walkthrough of the erase-and-replace option (the evidence gives only page titles), and explicit coverage of replacing operating systems other than Windows.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can install the OS in place of my current OS on the same machine

citations.quote: Download Ubuntu Desktop and replace your current operating system. It's easy to install in place of Windows, or run Ubuntu alongside it.
Installation: Create a bootable USB stick • Install Ubuntu Desktop
BitLocker during Ubuntu installation • Turn off BitLocker in Windows • Intel RST during Ubuntu installation • Reconfigure Windows to use AHCI
